title: Advancing animations for CollisionShapes multiple times a physics tick breaks the animation
body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible in 4.7 and 4.8 dev6

### System information

Godot v4.8.dev6 - Fedora Linux 44 (KDE Plasma Desktop Edition) on Wayland - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 1 monitor (2880x1920 @ 119.97 Hz) - Vulkan (Forward+) - integrated AMD Radeon 780M Graphics (RADV PHOENIX) - AMD Ryzen 7 7840U w/ Radeon  780M Graphics (16 threads) - 30.64 GiB memory - PulseAudio (44100 Hz, Stereo/mono)

### Issue description

This is an issue from a workaround to #123861 
Because it is not reliable right now to have animation tracks default to the values of the RESET animation, we are first playing the RESET animation, mixing it and then playing the intended animation.

This works well but animating CollisionShapes multiple times in a single physics tick break the animation.
The position, shape and disabled state of the CollisionShape might ignore the animation temporarily or entirely.

In the example MRP I am playing a "left" and "right" animation that is animating the respective shapes.
I also always first play the RESET animation an use `advance(0)` to make sure it is mixed.
If I switch back and forth between the animations without letting them finish, the CollisionShapes gets animated inconsistently. You can tell by them getting offset from the similar MeshInstance3D node.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d51e328e-bded-4cc7-a2a1-bb56bdccb782

It looks like there is no way to safely animate CollisionShape properties without potentially running into this issue.
That's why we are forced to use a custom tool class that extends the AnimationPlayer. The class offers placeholder properties that are animated instead and the `mixer_applied` signal is used to apply the changes to the real CollisionShape properties once.

### Steps to reproduce

See MRP.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

In this MRP I am brute forcing this bug to happen by doing the following steps when starting an animation:
1. Play the RESET animation
2. Use `advance(0)` to mix the animation result so it is actually resetting all the values
3. Play the intended animation
4. Again use `advance(0)` to immediately mix the result again (This seems unnecessary but makes sure that the CollisionShape properties are reliably mixed during the physics process instead of at the end of idle time)
[MRP_animating_collisions_bug.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32685673/MRP_animating_collisions_bug.zip)

Make sure to enable 'Visible Collision Shapes' before starting the game.

Once you do, try to play each animation in full with left arrow key and right arrow key.
Then try pressing them in quick succession alternatively and see how the CollisionShapes get inconsistent.

The expected result would be that animating the CollisionShape properties could be done without hitting these issues.
Maybe there is a proper way to animate them safely for immediate use in the physics process of the same frame?
